I bought a weight set for $35. I really like it. I can use it whenever I want, at my convenience. We all have hectic lives sometimes, and it's hard to make time to go to the gym. Having a weight set at home makes it harder to make excuses to not work out.

I still like hitting the gym, though. It's always good to be around people. You get an idea of how others look, how they're doing, what they're working out, and you can set standards for yourself and get motivated based on that. Plus... eye candy.

 

Some links to support my claims.

  • Gym: http://www.cnbc.com/id/26663228

  • Adjustable 40-lb Weight Set, $35: https://www.walmart.com/ip/Gold-s-Gym-40-lb-Adjustable-Dumbbell-Set/21672511

  • Adjustable 40-lb Weight Set, $22: https://www.walmart.com/ip/CAP-Barbell-40-Pound-Vinyl-Dumbbell-Set/19517002

  • Adjustable 100-lb Weight Set, $52: https://www.walmart.com/ip/US-Weight-100-lbs.-Traditional-Weight-Set/4404139

  • Look through this for more: https://www.walmart.com/search/?page=2&query=adjustable+weight+set&sort=rating_high#searchProductResult
Gym memberships cost $40-$50 dollars a month. An adjustable weight set from Walmart will cost ~$20-$50 static. Having a weight set at home can save time and money, though gyms offer a social setting.

TP006D Power Rack from Fitness Avenue for $229.99 I've personally used it for years, and outside of upgrading the safety bars, I've been very happy with my purchase:
https://www.fitnessavenue.ca/amstaff-tp006d-power-squat-rack-training-system-cage

Fitness Gear 300 lb. Olympic Weight Set from Dick's Sporting Goods for $219.99. The weights alone make this worth it, and the bar is a decent starter bar. You'll want to upgrade the bar later, though, and when you do, don't skimp out on it. The bar is one of the few places you don't want to slack on: https://www.dickssportinggoods.com/p/fitness-gear-300-lb-olympic-weight-set-16fgeu300lbstwth7brb/16fgeu300lbstwth7brb

Or, if you don't need to have brand new, you can go to second hand sporting goods stores, or Craigslist, and get equipment dirt cheap.

If all I'd ever had was weights at home I'd probably be a hopeless butterball by now, it's the interaction and competition with others at the gym that pushes me to do more. Everyone's different in this respect, what works for one person doesn't necessarily work for another.
You have access to a much larger array of equipment at the gym. Additionally the low budget no frills gyms are only about $10-$15 a month.
